---
title: "UC10 Document Anonymizer"
subtitle: "PDF / DOCX in → the same file out, people and target company masked, fully local"
---

Research with interviews, case files or theses runs into the same problem every time: the material names
people and the organisation the research was for, and it cannot be shared until those are removed. Doing
that by hand is slow and error-prone, and cloud anonymisation services mean sending the raw documents out
of the organisation first.

UC10 does it locally. A PDF or Word file goes in; the same file comes out with the names of people (and
their email, phone, student number and bank account) and the target company replaced by stable labels.
Layout, tables and fonts stay as they were. Everything else stays readable: other organisations, software,
places, dates, and the literature the document cites.

::: {.callout-important}
## Where UC10 stands (2026-10-01)
Working on the local stack: researchers drop files in `input/`, name the target company in
`input/targets.txt`, and get `output/<name>_anon.pdf` back, with the key in `keys/`. A 46-page thesis has
been processed as PDF and DOCX. The dry-run passes and the evaluation set shows 0 leaks of 44 and 0 false
positives. Not built yet: the audit trace, encrypted storage, and blocking internet access for the pipeline
containers. See [Workflow](workflow.qmd) and [Plan](plan.qmd).
:::

## What gets masked

| What | Example | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Person | Jan de Vries, later "De Vries" | PERSOON_1 |
| Target company | Acme Trailers, acmetrailers.nl | ORGANISATIE_1 |
| Student / employee number | S1234567 | ID_1 |
| Email address | jan@example.nl | EMAIL_1 |
| Phone number | 06-12345678 | TELEFOON_1 |
| Bank account | NL91ABNA0417164300 | IBAN_1 |

Not masked: other organisations, software (ERP, PLM), places, dates, job titles, and published references
("(Yin, 2018)" and the reference list). The target company is masked there too.

Labels are **global and stable**: the same person gets the same label in every document. Neo4j keeps a
SHA-256 hash of each value with its label; the value itself is never stored.

## Privacy design

- Everything runs on the local machine in Docker: Docling, the anonymizer and Neo4j. During a 46-page run
  every connection stayed inside the local Docker network; host ports listen on 127.0.0.1 only.
- Not yet enforced by the network: the containers could reach the internet. Blocking that is requested.
- The written file is read back; if any original is still in it, no file is produced.
- The key (`keys/`) reverses the anonymization, so it is personal data: it is kept apart from `output/` and out of git.
- The repo folder is synced by Nextcloud, so originals and keys also reach the Nextcloud server.
- A Dutch one-pager for users: `output/Onepager - lokaal anonimiseren.pdf`.

## Stack (local, 2026-10-01)

| Component | Service | Address |
|---|---|---|
| Document parsing | Docling (docling-serve v1.35, async API, no OCR) | localhost:5001 |
| Detection + rewriting | `uc10-anonymizer`: Presidio + spaCy `nl_core_news_lg`, `en_core_web_lg`; PyMuPDF | localhost:5010 |
| Label registry | Neo4j | bolt://localhost:7687 |
| Audit trail (planned) | Langfuse | localhost:3100 |
| Encrypted storage (planned) | MinIO bucket `doc-anonymizer` | server, currently down |

## Try it

```bash
# Anonymize everything in input/ (target company in input/targets.txt)
python3 scripts/anonymize_folder.py

# Checks
python3 tests/dry_run.py            # service, Docling, DOCX + PDF same-format output
python3 tests/eval_detection.py     # leaks and false positives on the evaluation texts
```

The service code is in `service/app.py`; the container is built by the localstack in InstallLocalAiPackage.
